name: Pol Pot
role: Leader of the Communist Party of Kampuchea and of Democratic Kampuchea (1975-1979)
summary: Led the Khmer Rouge to power in 1975 and ran Democratic Kampuchea as a one-party state that abolished money, markets, private property and religion, and evacuated the cities into collective cooperatives. His regime organised a centrally planned, self-reliant economy and a mass security apparatus, and it persecuted ethnic minorities and perceived enemies. In his own words he described the revolution as class struggle, rejected foreign investment and aid, and called the regime's policies a success.

sources.title: Democratic Kampuchea
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Overview of the regime's policies: the expulsion of Vietnamese, the suppression of minorities, the single official language and the state's control of the economy

universal-healthcare.rationale: Said each cooperative had a medical centre and that medical care reached the whole population, including remote areas.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Abolished private trade and ran exchange through the state and cooperatives, which he presented as the path of independence and collectivism; he never argued for markets.

public-ownership.rationale: In the 1978 Hong Kong interview he said the people had become the masters of the means of production, lands, animals and factories, which the state and cooperatives held.

property-fundamental.rationale: In the 1977 anniversary speech he said the aim was gradually eliminating the idea of private ownership, with collectivist and socialist ownership in its place.

worker-ownership.rationale: In the 1978 Hong Kong interview he described the people as masters of the factories and the means of production, held in collective form.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred: cadres were told to watch for enemy agents and lifestyle meetings enforced constant mutual vigilance; this implies tolerance of surveillance, but no statement addresses surveillance directly.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Said the regime had totally eliminated depravity, banditry, prostitution and toxicomania, which implies prohibition rather than legal use.

strong-leader.rationale: No stated position on a leader bypassing gridlock; one-party rule without elections is something nearby.

state-harmful.rationale: Built a strong, centralised state and said a socialist state should grow stronger rather than wither away while surrounded by enemies.

empower-police-military.rationale: Built a large Revolutionary Army and a security apparatus at S-21, and described the army as the guardian of the nation's territory.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Said the regime had completely wiped out prostitution and related crimes through its mass campaign.

decide-locally.rationale: The Plan asked base-area leaders to make local decisions, but policy was directed by the Party centre under democratic centralism.

rehabilitation.rationale: Enemies were arrested, tortured and executed at S-21 and in the zones, which the regime described as eradication rather than reform.

traditional-family.rationale: Collectivised eating, housing and childcare, which the Plan and its historians describe as aimed at smashing individualism and family loyalties.

more-religion-public.rationale: In the 1978 Belgian talks he said the problem of religion had been solved, with monks unfrocked and their number greatly reduced, and pagodas destroyed.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Said the new culture was national and progressive, preserving what was useful from national tradition and Angkor, while eliminating what was reactionary.

gradual-change.rationale: Pursued rapid and radical transformation ('great leaps and bounds') and abolished existing institutions rather than changing them gradually.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Expelled ethnic Vietnamese and closed the borders, which the record describes as reducing foreign presence.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Inferred: he presented the non-aligned movement as a source of support, but gave no view on giving the UN more power.

free-trade.rationale: Emphasised self-reliance and independence and refused foreign investment with political conditions, while still exporting rice.

nation-first.rationale: Said the country must put its own independence and interests first and decide its own destiny, rather than depend on foreign powers.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred: he condemned Vietnamese intervention as aggression, but no statement addresses intervention to protect human rights.

open-borders.rationale: Closed the country's borders and expelled foreigners, which contradicts open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Inferred: the regime rejected economic growth through foreign investment and focused on self-sufficiency, but growth itself was pursued by the Plan.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Inferred: he credited hydraulic works, medicine and technical training for solving the country's food and health problems, but not technology in general.

revolution-justified.rationale: Said the revolution was justified and that armed struggle against the old regime and its foreign backers was the people's just cause.

experts-over-public.rationale: Said the people were the fundamental factor and that technicians should be trained from the base, while professionals and intellectuals were persecuted.

central-planning.rationale: Adopted a centrally planned Four-Year Plan (1977-1980) setting targets for rice, rubber and industry, and called for it to be implemented from the Party centre.

socialized-markets.rationale: Trade was run by the state and cooperatives with private markets abolished; this is close to public ownership of trade but he did not state it as a principle.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Said the state would direct resources to agriculture first and then to industry, using rice exports to fund industrial development.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Collectivised farmland into cooperatives from 1973 and rejected small private holdings as remnants of the old capitalist order to be eliminated.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: In the 1977 anniversary speech he said cooperatives 'continue to operate without the use of money, with no daily salary', and in 1978 he described giving up money as the regime's practice; he left any future return to money to the people.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Abolished money entirely, which goes beyond the statement's market direction; he never addressed central banks or a market-set currency.

one-party-rule.rationale: Said the Communist Party of Kampuchea was the sole genuine leadership of the revolution and that state power rested on the Party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Denounced the monarchy as the enemy of the people and religion, and abolished it when the regime took power.

democracy-best.rationale: Presented the regime's version of 'broad democracy' under the Party's dictatorship as superior to the old freedoms.

workers-councils.rationale: Inferred: the cooperatives and workers' collectives were the organising units of the regime, but no statement names workers' councils as the basis of power.

political-violence-never.rationale: Said armed struggle is the highest form of struggle and that the Party applies the dictatorship of the proletariat to enemies, justifying violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: Said that the people's wartime struggle tempered their courage and patriotism, without saying war builds national character as such.

military-superiority.rationale: Said the army must defend the country and that Democratic Kampuchea would defeat Vietnamese aggression, which is not an aim of military superiority over rivals.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Presented the Kampuchean nation as a single people and classified and persecuted minorities whom it treated as outside it.

class-struggle-history.rationale: In the 1977 anniversary speech he presented Kampuchean history as a sequence of class struggles between exploiting and exploited classes.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Aimed to meet everyone's needs equally through communal eating and identical supply in the cooperatives.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Condemned individualism and private profit as moral failings and sought to eliminate self-interest through collective life.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Subordinated individual life to the collective through compulsory labour, collective eating and the Party's line.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Inferred: nature was treated as a resource for the revolution's production targets, with no statement that it has value in itself.

limit-population.rationale: Said the country had no reason to reduce or level its population and that population should be increased as quickly as possible.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Inferred: the regime rejected the old industrial and foreign-model economy, but he did not call industrial civilization a disaster.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Pursued rapid transformation with 'great leaps and bounds' in agriculture, hydraulic projects and industry, even where it disrupted existing institutions.

restore-past-order.rationale: Inferred: he rejected the old order of exploitation and aimed at a new society, though he also appealed to national traditions and past greatness.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Inferred: the Party insisted on a 'correct line' based on revolutionary principle, and judged policy by ideological fit as well as results.

direct-action.rationale: Said the revolution was won by armed struggle rather than through the elections of 1955 and 1958, which he described as rigged by the enemy.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Inferred: the regime pursued intensive rice cultivation and industrial production rather than a return to foraging, though it praised rural self-sufficiency.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Presented the mass line in which most people both studied and worked in production, which narrows the division of labour without abolishing it.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Food and goods were distributed by supply through the cooperatives and communal eating, not by wages or wealth, though he also tied supply to work.

production-for-use.rationale: Said production should meet the people's needs; the regime abolished trade for profit and organised production around the cooperatives.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Described capitalists and landlords as exploiting workers and peasants, and described the old economic system as based on exploitation that the revolution smashed.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: In the 1977 anniversary speech he said the Party applies the dictatorship of the proletariat to enemies and to the handful of reactionary elements.

collective-farming.rationale: In the 1977 anniversary speech he defended the collective peasant cooperatives as the base of national defence and food production.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Attributed aggression and war to imperialism and the exploiting classes, describing the US as leader of world imperialism.

conscription.rationale: Said everyone participates in production works and national defence, and the regime required all able people to serve in the army or the cooperatives.

total-state.rationale: Directed production, housing, eating, health, education and culture through the Party and the state, with collective life organised in every area.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Said 'we don't want even one inch of anyone else's land' and that Democratic Kampuchea had no need to annex anyone's territory.

single-common-good.rationale: Inferred: he defined one revolutionary line and the people's interest through the Party, rather than balancing the competing interests of groups.

national-self-determination.rationale: Said Kampuchea must decide its own destiny in independence and sovereignty, and that every nation has the right to its own independence.

force-without-un.rationale: Inferred: the regime used force against Vietnam and Thailand-facing enemies without seeking any outside authorisation.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Presented Marxism-Leninism and historical materialism as the scientific guide to the revolution, while rejecting religion.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Everyone who could work was required to labour in the cooperatives in return for food and shelter.

class-collaboration.rationale: Insisted that class struggle continues and that exploiters must be overthrown rather than cooperated with.

dominated-front.rationale: Inferred: he presented Kampuchea as a non-aligned country in solidarity with independence movements and oppressed peoples.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Described the old state as an instrument of feudal and capitalist ruling classes, to be replaced by a workers' and peasants' state.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The Plan pursued agriculture and hydropower rather than fossil fuels, and no statement addresses domestic oil, gas or coal production.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Forced minorities including the Cham and Chinese to adopt Khmer language and customs and broke up their separate communities.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The regime executed and persecuted people by class and ethnicity, treating some groups as enemies without the equal rights the statement describes.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Said the revolution was carried out 'in complete independence and by relying on our own resources', without making lasting socialism depend on revolution abroad.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Ended religious instruction and pagoda education and placed schooling inside the cooperatives and factories.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Said that the socialist state must defend itself against hostile neighbours and imperialists, and stressed defence of the country as a continuing task.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Said the people would decide whether the society was on the right path and could decide differently if unsatisfied, though the Party held power regardless.

trade-surplus.rationale: Said the regime exported rice and rubber to pay for imported machinery and industrial goods, which it treated as necessary for independence.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced ethnic Vietnamese and others out of the country and relocated minority groups under pressure.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Condemned competition among individuals and cooperatives as producing corruption and individualism, and said the competition was only for money.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Allowed only the Party to rule, banned other parties, and treated opposition parties as enemies to be eradicated.

separated-powers.rationale: Placed the state, courts and Party under a single Party leadership with no separation of powers.

vanguard-party.rationale: In the 1977 anniversary speech he said no people had won a revolution without a working-class party leading it, and that the CPK was that party.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Said the revolution served the poor peasants and the working classes who formed more than ninety per cent of the people.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Said Kampuchea had no reason to reduce or level off its population and should increase it as quickly as possible.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Inferred: he treated minority groups as enemies of the nation, but no statement claims diversity weakens cohesion in general.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Inferred: the regime appointed cadres through the Party and did not use lottery or election for offices.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Said there was no court to settle contradictions among the people and that the regime acted against enemies by its own measures, outside ordinary legal protections.

party-controls-media.rationale: State radio and the press were run as Party propaganda, with the Voice of Democratic Kampuchea used to broadcast the Party's line.

party-commands-army.rationale: Described the armed forces as the Party's military line and placed the Revolutionary Army under the Party's leadership and central committee.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Cadres, soldiers and workers had no salary in the regime, which he presented as collective equality.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Said decisions of the Party once debated and adopted must be carried out, under democratic centralism.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Insisted on independence and sovereignty as non-negotiable and rejected any union that would dissolve Kampuchean sovereignty.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Said reactionary and decadent culture must be eliminated and only progressive culture and songs kept, which is censorship on moral grounds.

people-in-arms.rationale: Inferred: the regime relied on a large armed militia alongside a regular army, but no statement favours an armed citizenry in place of a professional army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Said the cities were a threat and a centre of enemy power, and moved the urban population into the countryside to live in cooperatives.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Said the old education, copied from foreign systems, was incapable of serving the country and that technicians trained from the base served better than graduates.

death-penalty.rationale: The regime executed people it defined as enemies without trial, and said the Party must isolate and eradicate the cruellest enemies.

minority-language-support.rationale: Banned minority languages, including Chinese languages and the languages of more than twenty minorities, rather than supporting them.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Required everyone to dress uniformly like poor peasants and to live collectively, leaving no room for individual ways of living.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Said independence required transforming the economy, smashing the old production system and building new collective relations of production.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Suspended ordinary freedoms in pursuit of rapid economic development and said the democratic freedoms of the old order had served only the exploiting classes.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred: the regime rejected foreign aid and investment as a basis for development, and called for self-reliance.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Abolished private property in favour of collective ownership for the common good, which goes beyond the statement's limited justification.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Denounced the Vietnamese as annexationists and swallowers of territory, and said their occupation of Kampuchean land was unlawful.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Curbed the Buddhist institutions and placed the clergy under the regime, with monks sent to labour in the cooperatives.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Abolished the monarchy and called it the enemy of the people and of religion, rejecting sacred rulership.

character-from-environment.rationale: Described people as carrying the 'old class character' from their upbringing, which could be changed by education and collective life.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred: the regime's leaders ruled by Party decree with no legal limits, but no statement addresses a ruler being above law.

leader-cult.rationale: Busts of Pol Pot were produced in anticipation of a personality cult, but the cult was never realised; he presented himself modestly and used a pseudonym.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Said enemies and class contradictions remained under socialism and that the dictatorship of the proletariat must be applied to them.

land-redistribution.rationale: Collectivised land into cooperatives from 1973 and ended landlord ownership, with peasants working the land collectively.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The regime raised Kampuchea Krom as a historical grievance but did not claim territory on the basis of nationality in its public statements.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred: he presented Vietnam's Indochina Federation as an unacceptable union and rejected political union of neighbouring peoples.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Denied minority groups self-governing cultural institutions and schools, banned their languages and dispersed their communities.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Cited historical materialism while insisting that man is the determining factor in production and that the people's struggle drives change.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Pursued autarkic self-reliance and independence from foreign trade; the bloc with colonies is not addressed and rice exports continued.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred: he rejected foreign trade and foreign influence, but no statement addresses binding labour or environmental standards in trade agreements.

moral-incentives.rationale: Replaced wages with revolutionary spirit and collective duty as the spur to work, with no daily salary for cadres, soldiers or workers.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Described building an armed force from small guerrilla units and bases as the way the revolution was won, from 1968 onward.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Abolished the monarchy and the privileges of the old ruling classes as part of the revolution.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Presented the nation's own history and traditions as the basis of education, but the statement about school history is not addressed directly.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Denounced colonialism and imperialism as the exploitation of less developed peoples, which implies rejection of tutelage by advanced societies.

patriotic-education.rationale: Said children, youth and combatants received education in revolutionary patriotism and knew who were the friends and enemies of the revolution.

delink-world-market.rationale: Pursued self-reliance and withdrawal from foreign economic dependence rather than integration with the world market, while still exporting rice.

elective-rulers.rationale: The 1976 election was a single-list vote under the Party, so the regime held an election but did not choose rulers competitively.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The 1976 National Assembly was a one-party body under the Party, so parliament was not the supreme authority in practice.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Required everyone to take part in collective political life, including criticism and self-criticism sessions, and rejected withdrawal from public affairs.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Argued that the old culture served the exploiting classes but gave no account of mass culture pacifying the people.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Said poor countries had been plundered and oppressed by foreign imperialists, feudalists and colonialists, and that independence was needed to end it.

party-own-road.rationale: Said the regime followed its own road and did not follow the policies of other socialist states, including China and Vietnam.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Said Kampuchea should rely on its own resources, refused foreign investors and aid with political conditions, and made independence and self-reliance its central principle.

return-lost-territory.rationale: He denied claiming former territories in the 1978 Yugoslav interview but raised Kampuchea Krom and the lost islands as grounds for a claim the government chose not to press.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred: the army was described as defending the Party's revolution and the constitution, but no statement gives it a guardian role over civilian government.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: In the Plan's explanation he refused foreign investors, saying they would bring political entanglement, and aimed to keep the economy in national hands.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land was worked through state and cooperative structures and not held by individuals, as the constitution's state ownership of production implies.

single-official-language.rationale: Khmer was the only legally recognised language, and minority languages including Chinese and Vietnamese were banned.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Condemned individual accumulation and the pursuit of money and possessions as corrupting, and collectivised households in the cooperatives.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Refused foreign investment and aid because they would bring political entanglement, so foreign influence was restricted.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Said the population should grow to 15-20 million, but gave no financial incentives, so the mechanism is not addressed.

job-guarantee.rationale: Compulsory labour in the cooperatives gave everyone work, though not framed as an employer-of-last-resort guarantee.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Accused the Vietnamese and ethnic minorities such as the Cham of conspiring against the revolution as enemy agents, and treated them as the nation's enemies.

local-production.rationale: Organised food and goods production within cooperatives close to where people lived, using local materials for medicine and workshops.

informal-organisation.rationale: Inferred: he organised the movement through a disciplined Party with committees and central structures, not small informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Said foreign policy and independence were stipulated in the constitution, and that Kampuchea would decide its own destiny.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Insisted that Kampuchea would not accept foreign domination and would not pay tribute to any leading power.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Collectivised clothing, housing and food, so personal belongings were not kept private; the regime allowed few personal items.

religion-illusion.rationale: Said the problem of religion had been solved by itself as material conditions changed, though he did not describe religion as an illusion.

socialized-care.rationale: Collectivised eating, clothing and housing into communal arrangements, and set up schools and kitchens inside the cooperatives.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Organised society into cooperatives of several hundred families holding property in common, with local collective structures.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred: the regime moved and dispersed populations for its own purposes rather than encouraging majority settlement, though policy of settlement is not addressed.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred: he cited Kampuchea's historical borders and the lost islands as a legal and historical basis, which is a limited form of historical claim.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Suppressed political opposition and independent organisations, and purged Party members and cadres accused of treachery, according to the record.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Said the people should take part directly in decisions in workplaces and communities through the mass line and democratic centralism.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: No stated position on the left-right division; presenting the Party line as the only correct one is something nearby.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Monks and people were ordered to wear peasant black clothing and the uniform dress of the cooperatives, and religious dress was banned.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Built and expanded a standing army and said the Revolutionary Army was essential to defending the country.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Said the country pursued 'independence, sovereignty, neutrality and nonalignment' and that its friends included non-aligned countries.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred: the regime refused foreign loans and investment with political conditions, which is in line with refusing lender conditions.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred: the regime targeted Chinese merchants and traders as exploiters associated with capitalism, which fits a policy of boycotting minority shops.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The regime enforced state atheism and Buddhist monks were treated as a special class to be reduced, according to the record.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred: he rejected foreign influence and interference, but no statement addresses foreign bases on national territory.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Pay was abolished and supply was given by collective work; the statement's contrast with ownership is only loosely reflected.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Traced Kampuchea's history of more than 2,000 years through successive social stages, presenting the nation as continuous.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: In the 1977 anniversary speech he called for the heroes and martyrs who died for the revolution to be honoured and their memory kept.

culture-before-state.rationale: The speeches give culture an important role, but no statement sets cultural renewal before state building.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Said the working class and its Party must hold political power, and that the Party was the sole leadership of the socialist revolution.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Water works, hospitals and local services were run by the state and cooperatives as collective services.

anonymous-payments.rationale: No stated position on untraceable payments; abolishing money is something nearby.

person-over-state.rationale: Treated people as means to the revolution and the collective, sacrificing individuals to the cooperatives and the Party's aims.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Presented politics as the cultivation of the people's material and moral life, without stating that people have a spiritual nature.

dense-cities.rationale: Evacuated the populations of Phnom Penh and other cities to the countryside, and treated cities as a source of enemy power and corruption.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred: the regime treated ethnic minorities as enemies rather than as groups with legitimate political interests.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred: he spoke of the 'race' and national honour of Kampuchea and defended national pride, but not racial pride as such.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: He said Democratic Kampuchea had no reason to aggress, but the regime raided Vietnamese territory and the claim is disputed in the record.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Said Vietnam was pursuing an Indochina Federation to take possession of Kampuchea, dissolve its nationality and make it part of Vietnam.

capital-controls.rationale: Kept the economy closed to foreign capital and tightly controlled the movement of money and foreign exchange through the state.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred: the Party's army and militia were the armed forces, though armed guerrilla units were also raised in the countryside.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred: the army was disciplined under the Party and required to fight the enemies it was assigned, with no provision for refusal.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Said the old production system and state machinery were smashed and replaced by the revolution, rather than taken over.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred: the Plan measured natural resources in production and export targets, but did not frame them as capital valued in the economy.

sacred-nation.rationale: Inferred: the speeches present the nation as a sacred struggle to be defended, but no statement calls it a sacred community outliving its members.

workers-own-party.rationale: Said the working class needed its own party to lead the revolution, which the Communist Party of Kampuchea claimed to be.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Required minorities to adopt the Khmer language and customs and banned their own languages.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred: the regime suppressed all religion rather than granting equal recognition to several interpretations.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Said everyone wanted democratic freedoms but that they had belonged to the exploiters, and presented the regime's own rule as the genuine form of freedom.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Said a socialist state with nationalised property and a planned economy must be defended against capitalist restoration and foreign attack.

national-church-status.rationale: Ended the special status of Buddhism as the national religion and abolished its institutions.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Ended the autonomy of minority regions and dispersed their people into cooperatives, according to the record.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Said Democratic Kampuchea would keep the borders Vietnam had recognised in 1966-67 and did not claim former territories, though he also cited the lost islands and Kampuchea Krom.

simple-living.rationale: Pursued a rural, self-sufficient life of cooperatives and peasant labour, with city life and consumer goods discouraged.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred: he framed the defence of the nation's territory and ancestors' struggles as a sacred duty, without a stated spiritual bond to the land.

close-ties-china.rationale: Said China was Kampuchea's main partner and that Mao's China was a source of support, which he praised in the speeches on Mao.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Held the lands, forests, rivers and resources in common through the state and cooperatives, with individual appropriation eliminated.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred: he combined modern technical training with national tradition, such as local medicine and traditional methods.

national-resource-control.rationale: Said the country's resources and economy must be under the Kampuchean people's own control, independent of foreign interests.

notes: Positions are drawn from his speeches and interviews (1976-1978, compiled in Pol Pot Selected Works, Volume 1, and the Four-Year Plan documents) and from the record of policies he drove, described secondhand in Wikipedia and in the Yale volume's introductions. His 1997 interview with Nate Thayer is known only through news summaries; the 1976 constitution's text was not opened, and its provisions are taken from secondhand summaries. Most of the statement list is not addressed by his speeches or the record and is answered null. Atrocities (S-21, the purges, the expulsion of Vietnamese, the killing of Cham and Chinese) are recorded in the secondhand sources and are not presented as his stated views, but they are the record of policies he personally drove and are reflected in the answers where a statement matches.
